title: Nvidia to report Q3 earnings after the bell with Colette Kress to host first call as interim CEO
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Nvidia’s earnings call could become the business event of the year. The numbers will matter, but the bigger question is whether the company powering the artificial intelligence boom can command the same confidence without Jensen Huang at the microphone.

When interim CEO Colette Kress addresses investors, she will face an audience stretching far beyond Nvidia shareholders. Technology executives, chip suppliers, fund managers and startup founders will be listening for clues about the next chapter of an industry built on enormous spending and even bigger expectations.

First comes the financial scorecard: revenue, margins, demand and guidance. Investors will scrutinize whether customers continue buying advanced chips at a pace that justifies the infrastructure commitments surrounding AI. Strong results would provide reassurance. A cautious outlook could intensify questions already hanging over the sector.

Then comes the leadership test. Kress must explain how Nvidia will make decisions, sustain customer relationships and protect its competitive position during the transition. Her answers about investment discipline, partnerships and the search for a permanent CEO could prove as consequential as any earnings figure.

That combination makes this call extraordinary. A routine quarterly presentation has become a public examination of corporate resilience, succession planning and the durability of the AI economy.

Calling it the event of the year is a bold judgment, but the stakes support the argument: few corporate briefings bring together leadership uncertainty, technological competition and such widespread financial exposure.

The most revealing moment may come during questions from analysts. Can Kress replace uncertainty with a credible operating plan?

Investors will watch her tone, the specificity of her commitments and the assumptions behind guidance. Confidence earned through clear answers could shape how markets judge Nvidia and its partners for months.

For one evening, Wall Street’s biggest AI debate will have a single microphone. Colette Kress will be holding it.
